column1: # Gao T., Shen T., Lin W., Gu A., Ju Y. (2012). Experimental Determination of CO2 Solubility in Liquid CH4/N2 Mixtures at
# Cryogenic Temperatures. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 51, 9403-9408. doi:10.1021/ie3002815. ACS copyright, owner-provided.
# Tables 2 (p. 9406) and 4 (p. 9407), read from 170-200 dpi renders.
# System: solid CO2 + saturated liquid (static-analytic SLE, GC analysis; the liquid is at its bubble point, so these are
# three-phase points with vapour present, vapour not sampled). Solvent N2 fraction is the CO2-free feed composition.
# block BIN = Table 2, CO2 solubility in pure liquid CH4: x in 10^3 ppm (as printed; x_CO2 = value x 1e-3), with Davis et al.
#   1962 values xexp (10^3 ppm) and delta = 100 (x - xexp)/xexp at seven of the temperatures; MRD 4.39 %. NO PRESSURE printed
#   (Maltby 2025 therefore lists only the 32 ternary points). 9 points, -160 to -103.3 C (113.2 to 169.9 K).
#   NOTE: xexp are the Davis 1962 Table 4 crystal points (-226.3 to -153.9 F = -143.5 to -103.3 C; 0.16 mol % = 1.6 x 10^3
#   ppm). At -103.3 C Gao prints 29.0 where Davis prints 2.94 mol % (29.4 x 10^3 ppm); not reconciled.
# block N2_10/N2_30/N2_50/N2_70 = Table 4, CO2 solubility in CH4/N2 mixtures with 10, 30, 50, 70 % N2: p in kPa (equilibrium
#   pressure as printed), x in ppm (mole fraction x 1e6), xcal = their PR EOS calculation (kij CH4/CO2 T-dependent, N2/CO2
# Uncertainty (section 2): temperature accuracy +-0.05 C, pressure relative 0.1 %, GC total relative 1.1 % (TCD) and
#   1.6 % (FID), repeatability of the ten samples per point within 3 %; standard-gas purity 1 % of label (1 ppm absolute
# T_K is derived here (C + 273.15), not printed.
# Sanity check: x falls monotonically as T falls in every block, and p falls with T.
# Digits as printed, one sanity check, not re-verified (owner: not looking for 100 % correct data).
# Role: G5 low-temperature liquidus in CH4 and the N2 domain. Transcribed 2026-09-25, batch 2026-09-24-coolprop-low-temperature.
